items.title: ci: harden security guard trust boundary
items.body:
## Summary

- Split the CI Security Guard workflow into PR and trusted-repository execution paths.
- On `pull_request`, checkout trusted base code into `trusted-guard` and candidate PR code into `candidate-repo` with `persist-credentials: false`.
- Run the guard script from `trusted-guard/scripts/security/check_no_self_hosted_pull_request.py` against `candidate-repo/.github/workflows`.
- Block PR changes to the guard workflow, guard script, and guard tests by default so guard implementation changes require trusted maintainer handling.
- Add a workflow integrity regression test that fails if the PR path starts using candidate guard code again.

## Root Cause

The guard workflow previously ran on `pull_request`, checked out the candidate workspace, then executed the guard script and tests from that candidate checkout. A malicious PR could modify both workflow files and the guard implementation to make unsafe workflow changes pass.

## Validation

- `python3 tests/security/test_check_no_self_hosted_pull_request.py`
- `python3 tests/security/test_ci_security_guard_workflow_integrity.py`
- `python3 scripts/security/check_no_self_hosted_pull_request.py .github/workflows`

items.title: harden paper workspace tenant isolation
items.body:
## Summary

This PR hardens Paper Workspace tenant isolation across the service-role read path and authenticated Supabase/RLS access.

The leak path was that the paper workspace route authenticated the learner and passed `userId` into the read service, but topic artifacts were loaded through the service client by topic only. Because service-role access bypasses RLS, same-topic artifacts from another learner could be folded into paper workspace pinned summaries and topic workspace residency projections. The SQL paper workspace projection had the same topic-only join against `learning_artifacts`.

## Changes

- Adds learner ownership to `learning_artifacts` with `user_id`, backfilled from `learning_sessions.user_id` and `attempts.user_id` where those source links exist.
- Adds a learner/topic/residency index for artifact reads.
- Makes `listArtifactsByTopic` fail closed without `userId` and filter by both `user_id` and `canonical_home_topic_id`.
- Threads authenticated `userId` through paper workspace reads, legacy topic workspace reads, artifact lifecycle patching, paper entry artifact resolution, and session artifact anchors.
- Recreates learner-facing workspace views with `security_invoker = true`.
- Fixes `learning_paper_workspace_projection` so pinned artifact summaries join artifacts by both topic and learner ownership: `a.canonical_home_topic_id = ts.topic_id` and `a.user_id = pw.user_id`.
- Adds RLS policies for paper workspaces, paper topic sections, topic workspaces, workspace slots, artifacts, and artifact content versions.
- Adds regression and schema-contract tests for same-topic cross-user artifact isolation.

## Validation

items.title: feat: run Codex worker visual QA for generated MS screenshots (#1491)
items.body:
Closes #1491.

Visual QA gate for the 424 page-level MS screenshots generated in #1490. No screenshot may become a student-display candidate without a `visual_qa_pass` recorded here.

## What was actually inspected

All 424 screenshots were regenerated locally (byte-identical to #1490 — all 424 image hashes match the manifest) and visually inspected across 24 contact sheets, plus full-resolution review of the 25 pages backing student-display candidate rows.

Sheets are grouped by page orientation and letterboxed. CIE mark-scheme content pages are A4 landscape while cover pages are portrait, so a fixed portrait cell would have drawn every landscape page at half linear resolution and made the legibility judgement depend on page shape rather than on the render.

Three evidence layers are kept deliberately apart:

1. **Deterministic pixel pre-checks** — blankness, geometry against each page's own source PDF viewport, hash provenance, colour-overlay geometry. Mechanical; never grants a pass.
2. **Codex worker visual inspection** of every generated screenshot. The only layer that can see a page is the *wrong* page while still being a perfectly good render.
3. **Codex worker row/page alignment**, reading printed question labels off each page's Question column.

The upstream locator (#1489) was produced by a question-label regex over the PDF text layer. Re-reading that text layer here would only re-confirm the evidence that produced the locator under review, so it is deliberately not done. No OCR, no VLM, no external model call at any layer.

## Counts

| Status | Count |
| --- | --- |
| `visual_qa_pass` | 407 |
| `visual_qa_fail` | 6 |
| `visual_qa_blocked` | 11 |
| `needs_manual_review` | 0 |
| **total** | **424** |

Row/page alignment: `row_page_match_pass` 28, `page_correct_but_target_not_visible` 0, `wrong_page` 6, `needs_manual_review` 0.

## Release scope is conservative by default

Because nothing is legally authorized, promotion lands in a closed scope: `internal_only`, `requires_login: true`, `public_indexing_allowed: false`. `public_launch` is `future_authorization_required`. The validator fails if any public scope is granted without an authorization artifact, if indexing is enabled anywhere, if a closed scope drops login, or if an eligible asset has no release scope.

#1458 recorded `blocked` for these assets on the basis that no student-display legal authorization artifact exists. items.title: Fix learning runtime event RLS isolation
items.body:
## Summary
- Adds a Supabase migration enabling RLS on learner-sensitive learning runtime, event pipeline, delivery, mastery, review, session, reconciliation, and question-analysis event tables.
- Adds authenticated SELECT-own policies for direct learner-owned rows and parent-owner SELECT policies for child rows.
- Keeps `learning_question_analysis_snapshots` deny-direct and treats `learning_question_registry_projection` as service-layer/internal because it can expose `question_bank.prompt_representation` and `question_bank.provenance_summary`.
- Revokes direct `PUBLIC`/`anon`/`authenticated` access to `learning_question_registry_projection` and grants projection SELECT to `service_role` for backend paths.
- Keeps learner-facing session/review projections as `security_invoker = true` so base-table RLS applies.
- Extends the learning schema contract test to prevent missing RLS, broad direct writes, unsafe snapshot policies, and unsafe projection exposure regressions.

## Tables Protected
- Event pipeline: `learning_events`, `learning_event_effects`, `attempt_pipeline_state`
- Event delivery: `learning_event_deliveries`
- Runtime learner state: `learning_sessions`, `learning_session_lineage`, `learning_review_tasks`, `learning_family_masteries`, `learning_type_masteries`
- Nearby runtime/internal tables: `learning_reconciliation_runs`, `learning_question_analysis_snapshots`, `learning_question_events`
- Projections: `learning_question_registry_projection` direct-denied for browser roles; `learning_session_resume_projection` and `learning_review_queue_projection` remain security-invoker learner projections.

## Policy Model
- Direct owner: `user_id` or `learner_id` must equal `(select auth.uid())` for authenticated SELECT.
- Parent owner: `learning_event_effects` reads through owned `learning_events`; `learning_session_lineage` reads through owned child or parent sessions.
- Deny-direct: ownerless/internal tables have RLS enabled with no anon/authenticated policies rather than guessing ownership from topic, question, family, type, or paper fields.
- Registry projection: direct learner access is denied; learner-facing question access must go through API endpoints with explicit visibility filtering.
- Direct authenticated INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE remains closed for these append-only/internal learning tables.

## Service Role
Backend service-role paths remain operational. The migration grants `service_role` SELECT on the internal registry projection and does not rely on RLS for service-role protection.

## Codex Security Scan Findings Remediated
- Learning event tables lack RLS isolation
- Learning runtime tables lack RLS isolation
- Learning delivery table lacks RLS protections

items.title: chore: install git hooks from trusted runtime snapshot
items.body:
## Summary

Replaces mutable worktree-based local hook execution with trusted installed hook artifacts under Git metadata.

- Adds `scripts/git-hooks/install-trusted-hooks.js` to copy `scripts/git-hooks/guardrails.js` into `.git/ciecopilot-hooks/guardrails.js` and generate trusted hook artifacts.
- Generated `.git/hooks/pre-commit` and `.git/hooks/pre-push` files are POSIX shell wrappers that call the fixed trusted runner `.git/ciecopilot-hooks/hook-runner.cjs` with `"$@"`.
- The trusted `.cjs` runner uses CommonJS, verifies the SHA256 of `.git/ciecopilot-hooks/guardrails.js`, dynamically imports the ESM runtime, and calls `runtime.main(['--hook', hookName, ...argv])`.
- Keeps `npm run git:hooks:install` as the public installer entry point through the existing `scripts/git-hooks/install.sh` shim.
- Changes committed `.githooks/pre-commit` and `.githooks/pre-push` to fail closed and explain that `.githooks` are templates, not trusted enforcement.
- Updates workflow hook-install checks and docs to use `.git/hooks` plus `.git/ciecopilot-hooks/guardrails.js` instead of the old `.git/ao-hooks` copy path.

## Security Boundary

The previous installed hook flow copied committed `.githooks` wrappers that executed `node scripts/git-hooks/guardrails.js ...` from the active worktree. In task branches, PR worktrees, and agent worktrees, that guardrail code is mutable by the same branch being checked.

This PR moves the installed enforcement runtime into Git metadata. A branch can still edit the convenience source files, but installed hooks execute the trusted runner and runtime snapshot under `.git/ciecopilot-hooks/` until a developer intentionally reinstalls hooks from a trusted baseline. If the runtime snapshot changes after installation, the runner fails closed and asks the developer to reinstall trusted hooks.

This does not claim local hooks are a complete boundary against a user who can directly edit `.git/hooks`; it specifically blocks branch/worktree-controlled guardrail mutation from silently changing installed hook behavior.

## Regression Tests

Adds `tests/git-hooks/trusted-hooks.test.js` to verify:

- committed `.githooks/pre-commit` and `.githooks/pre-push` do not directly call `scripts/git-hooks/guardrails.js`;
- generated `.git/hooks/*` files are shell wrappers, do not use `NODE_OPTIONS` or `--experimental-default-type`, and call only `.git/ciecopilot-hooks/hook-runner.cjs`;
- the trusted `.cjs` runner verifies checksum success and fails closed on mismatch without `NODE_OPTIONS`;
- the installer writes trusted hooks only inside a temp Git metadata directory and does not write `.git/hooks/package.json`;
- existing pre-commit and pre-push evaluator behavior still blocks protected branches and dirty pushes.

items.title: security: restrict mark decision RPC to trusted callers
items.body:
## Root cause

`public.insert_mark_decisions(uuid, jsonb)` is a caller-controlled `SECURITY DEFINER` function in the exposed `public` schema. PostgreSQL gives newly created functions `PUBLIC EXECUTE` by default. The effective migration history never revoked that privilege, so `PUBLIC`, `anon`, and `authenticated` could invoke the RPC and supply both an arbitrary mark run ID and forged decision values while the function executed with its owner's RLS-bypassing privileges.

The effective function also had no fixed `search_path`, leaving a separate `function_search_path_mutable` issue.

The server-side marking route did not forward client-supplied `decisions` or `mark_run_id`: it resolved the rubric, ran the trusted decision engine, and created/reused the attempt and mark run server-side. However, a directly related confused-deputy gap existed because `evaluate-v1` called `resolveUserId(req)` without forcing JWT mode. When `EVIDENCE_LEDGER_ENABLED !== true`, the helper could accept `body.user_id` even though the route still performed service-role ledger writes.

## Effective database privilege before/after

### Before

| Capability | PUBLIC | anon | authenticated | service_role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Execute `insert_mark_decisions(uuid,jsonb)` | yes (default ACL) | yes (via PUBLIC) | yes (via PUBLIC) | yes (via PUBLIC/owner context) |
| Direct INSERT into `mark_decisions` | no | no | no | trusted policy/bypass path |

RLS was enabled on `attempts`, `mark_runs`, and `mark_decisions`, but that did not protect the definer RPC.

### After

| Capability | PUBLIC | anon | authenticated | service_role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Execute canonical RPC | no | no | no | explicit yes |
| Execute any same-name overload | no | no | no | only the canonical signature is granted |
| Direct INSERT into `mark_decisions` | no | no | no | unchanged |

The canonical function remains `SECURITY DEFINER`, now with `SET search_path = ''`. Its non-catalog table reference is `public.mark_decisions`, and its catalog function/type references are schema-qualified.

## Function definitions and overload audit

All checked-in historical definitions were reviewed in migration order:

1. `20260217100002_create_mark_decisions_table.sql`
   - creates `public.insert_mark_decisions(uuid,jsonb)`
   - returns six decision fields
   - `SECURITY DEFINER`
   - no fixed `search_path`
2. `20260220120000_phase2_marking_contract.sql`
   - drops/recreates the same identity signature
   - adds `alignment_confidence` and `evidence_spans` to the returned row
   - no fixed `search_path`
3. `20260221030815_phase2_marking_contract.sql`
   - repeats the same drop/recreate
   - is the effective pre-remediation definition
   - no fixed `search_path`

No checked-in overload other than `(uuid,jsonb)` was found. The new migration nevertheless enumerates every matching `pg_catalog.pg_proc` row and revokes untrusted EXECUTE privileges from all same-name overloads. The role test injects a synthetic `(text,jsonb)` overload before replaying the remediation and proves that the sweep closes it.

The migration-order contract test reads every migration in filename order. A later unsafe redefinition, exact grant, blanket function grant, or direct table INSERT grant causes the test to fail.

## Caller analysis

Legitimate runtime and migration callers remain compatible:

- `api/marking/lib/decision-writer.js` receives the backend service-role client and calls the canonical RPC for transactional batch insertion.
- `scripts/migration/backfill-mark-decisions.js` constructs its client from a service-role key and calls the same canonical RPC.
- `api/lib/supabase/pg-compat-client.js` uses a trusted server database connection and calls `SELECT * FROM public.insert_mark_decisions($1::uuid, $2::jsonb)`.
- Unit/property callers in the evidence-ledger tests retain the same RPC name, arguments, returned fields, and error semantics.
- `scripts/phase2/check_db_contract.py` only checks function existence.

The unique `(mark_run_id, rubric_id)` constraint, reason/alignment validation constraints, atomic INSERT statement, and eight-field return contract are unchanged.

## Server-side confused deputy

A narrow confused-deputy condition was found and fixed.

The client cannot select an arbitrary existing `mark_run_id` and cannot replace the trusted engine's `decisions`; those request fields are not forwarded. The mark run is created/reused from server-side ledger state.

The route could nevertheless accept an untrusted body `user_id` when the ledger feature flag was false while still writing via service role. `evaluate-v1` now calls:

```js
resolveUserId(req, { requireJwt: true })
```

This binds the attempt/mark-run chain to a verified request identity without changing scoring behavior or converting the service-only RPC into an `auth.uid()`-owned RPC.

## Migration strategy

Added forward-only migration:

`20260711065853_restrict_mark_decision_rpc_to_trusted_callers.sql`

It:

1. recreates the compatible canonical function with an empty fixed search path and qualified references;
2. enumerates all same-name overloads via `pg_catalog.pg_proc` / `pg_catalog.pg_namespace`;
3. revokes EXECUTE from `PUBLIC`, `anon`, and `authenticated` on every overload;
4. explicitly repeats the canonical revoke;
5. grants only the canonical `(uuid,jsonb)` signature to `service_role`.

Historical migrations were not modified, deleted, or rewritten.

## Tests run and exact results

### TDD red/green

- Initial focused run: 2 suites failed as expected; 4 security assertions failed and 31 existing assertions passed.
- After the remediation: 2 suites passed; 35/35 tests passed.

### Final JavaScript regression run

Command covered every `tests/evidence-ledger/*.test.js`, every marking test, PG compat, and Supabase audit-core:

- 27 suites passed
- 422 tests passed
- 0 snapshots
- exit 0

This includes:

- `tests/evidence-ledger/decision-writer.test.js`
- `tests/evidence-ledger/decision-writer.pbt.test.js`
- backfill unit/property tests
- ledger orchestrator/repository/auth/context tests
- marking route/engine/contract tests
- `api/lib/supabase/__tests__/pg-compat-client.test.js`

### Database role and migration verification

Using a fresh isolated local `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` container:

- bootstrapped only test Supabase roles/auth stubs;
- replayed all checked-in migrations in filename order;
- skipped only `20260118090900_008_rag_log_retention.sql` because the image lacks `pg_cron`, matching the existing CI rule;
- full replay exited 0;

- verified PUBLIC denial;
- verified anon denial;
- verified authenticated denial for an owner-bound mark run;
- verified authenticated denial for another user's mark run;
- verified service_role success and returned field compatibility;
- verified synthetic overload revocation;
- verified fixed empty search path;
- verified anon/authenticated direct INSERT denial.

Repository local catalog audit:

- catalog error count: 0

- `security_definer: true`
- `search_path_fixed: true`

- `executable_by_authenticated: false`

Supabase Security Advisors ran against the isolated local database with exit 0. They no longer report `insert_mark_decisions` for mutable search path or anon/authenticated definer execution. Existing unrelated advisor findings remain deliberately out of scope.

Additional checks:

- direct ESLint on changed JS: exit 0
- workflow YAML parse: exit 0
- `git diff origin/main --check`: exit 0
- final `npm run workflow:codex-preflight -- --json`: `top_status=healthy`, clean worktree, upstream ahead/behind 0

## Review follow-up (2026-07-11)

The JWT-only route boundary remains in place. Phase1 E2E now uses the fixed, non-sensitive local-only value `phase1-e2e-local-only-jwt-secret-not-for-production`; the smoke signs a five-minute access token whose `sub` is the fixture user, sends it as a Bearer token, and does not include `body.user_id` on the valid request. The migration-defined auth trigger was audited, and the seed now explicitly normalizes the fixture profile to active/student. The auth middleware preserves the full production profile projection and falls back to migration-defined columns only when PostgreSQL reports an undefined optional column, keeping plain-Postgres PG compat coverage intact.

The role SQL now has two isolated phases. It first asserts the untouched final catalog immediately after full migration replay, then rolls back runtime fixtures. A separate transaction creates an unsafe default-PUBLIC `(text,jsonb)` overload, proves that PUBLIC/anon/authenticated can execute it before remediation, reapplies the remediation, proves the sweep removes those privileges, and rolls back the overload.

The migration-order contract recognizes every `CREATE FUNCTION` or `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.insert_mark_decisions` regardless of language, return shape, or overload signature. Any later definition must restore `SECURITY DEFINER`, empty `search_path`, the all-overload untrusted-role sweep, and the canonical service-role grant.

PR-safe evidence now runs in DB Contract Gate as the GitHub-hosted `Mark Decision RPC Security Contract` job. It uses `ubuntu-latest`, a local `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` service, no repository secrets, full migration replay, the static effective-order test, and final-catalog/role assertions. The workflow filters include both security test files.

items.title: security: restrict evidence context RPC to trusted callers
items.body:
## Root cause

`public.get_evidence_context(uuid, ltree, integer)` was a caller-controlled `SECURITY DEFINER` function in the exposed `public` schema. Its historical migration explicitly granted `authenticated` EXECUTE and left PostgreSQL's default PUBLIC EXECUTE intact. The function accepted arbitrary `p_user_id` and did not bind it to `auth.uid()`, so a direct authenticated PostgREST caller could execute with the function owner's privileges and bypass self-only RLS on the evidence-ledger tables.

The effective function also used `SET search_path = public`, so it did not meet the fixed-empty search-path contract for privileged functions.

## Sensitive data exposed

An authenticated caller could request another learner's UUID and read:

- mastery from `user_learning_profiles.mastery_by_node`;
- misconception frequencies/tags from `user_learning_profiles.misconception_frequencies`;
- recent mark decisions joined through `attempts`, `mark_runs`, and `mark_decisions`;
- recent error events from `error_events`.

## Effective function definitions and overload audit

All checked-in migrations were read in filename order and the complete history was replayed into a disposable local PostgreSQL 16 database.

Before remediation there was exactly one same-name function:

- source: `20260219120000_create_get_evidence_context_rpc.sql`
- identity: `public.get_evidence_context(uuid,ltree,integer)`
- arguments: `p_user_id uuid, p_topic_path ltree, p_limit integer DEFAULT 10`
- result: `jsonb`
- language: `plpgsql`
- owner: `postgres`
- `SECURITY DEFINER`
- `search_path=public`

No other checked-in overload or redefinition existed. The remediation nevertheless enumerates every matching `pg_catalog.pg_proc` row so an unexpected or future overload cannot retain an executable bypass.

## Database privileges before and after

| Role | Before canonical EXECUTE | After canonical EXECUTE |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PUBLIC | yes (default ACL) | no |
| anon | yes (via PUBLIC) | no |
| authenticated | yes (default + explicit grant) | no |
| service_role | yes | explicit yes |

After full replay, the final catalog contains one canonical overload, owner `postgres`, `SECURITY DEFINER`, exact `search_path=""`, with PUBLIC/anon/authenticated denied and service_role allowed. The migration also removes service_role from every noncanonical overload before re-granting only the canonical signature.

No underlying sensitive-table grants or policies are changed by this PR.

## Caller inventory

- `api/evidence/context.js`: direct runtime caller. Normal server mode uses `getServiceClient()` backed by the service-role key. `SUPABASE_PG_COMPAT` mode uses the direct PostgreSQL compatibility client; that client returns `PG_COMPAT_RPC_UNSUPPORTED`, and the route uses its existing owner-filtered composed query fallback.
- `api/learning/lib/session-runtime/ask-context-builder.js`: direct runtime caller. It receives the service client from the authenticated Learning Session Ask path.
- `api/learning/sessions/[id]/ask.js`: indirect caller through `api/rag/lib/ask/ask-learning-session-wrapper.js`.
- `api/evidence/__tests__/context.test.js`: mock client.
- `tests/evidence/context-contract.test.js`: mocked service client.
- `tests/evidence-ledger/context-query.test.js` and `context-query.pbt.test.js`: mocked Supabase clients exercising the fallback.
- `api/rag/__tests__/helpers/ask-service-supabase-fixtures.js`: mock client used by Learning Session Ask tests.

No frontend/browser code and no script directly calls `get_evidence_context`.

## API route identity binding

`/api/evidence/context`:

- forces `resolveUserId(req, { requireJwt: true })`;
- takes `userId` only from the verified JWT result;
- does not parse query/body `user_id`;
- passes the verified user ID as RPC `p_user_id`;
- includes the verified user ID in the cache key;
- loads optional sessions with `(session_id, verified userId)`;
- loads workspaces with `(topic_id, verified userId)`;
- filters the composed fallback's profile, attempts, and errors by the verified user ID.

Regression tests cover missing/invalid JWT, forged body/query identities, RPC parameters, cache-key separation, and owner-filtered session/workspace lookups.

## Learning Session confused-deputy analysis

The Ask route authenticates first, then calls `readLearningSession(client, { userId: auth.userId, sessionId })`. The repository query filters both `session_id` and `user_id`. Another learner's session ID therefore returns `session_not_found` before AskAI or the evidence RPC runs.

`ask-context-builder` receives the persisted, owner-checked session and derives RPC `p_user_id` only from `session.user_id`. `clientContext.user_id` is ignored. Workspace projection reads use the same persisted session owner.

No cross-user confused-deputy path was found. A directly related error-boundary gap was fixed: only positively identified missing/unavailable RPC codes (`42883`, `PGRST202`, and `PG_COMPAT_RPC_UNSUPPORTED`) may use compatibility behavior. Permission errors, undefined-table errors, and unexpected RPC failures now fail closed instead of silently entering fallback/empty-context behavior.

## Selected migration design

Forward-only migration:

`20260711094331_restrict_evidence_context_rpc_to_trusted_callers.sql`

It:

1. recreates the compatible canonical function with `SECURITY DEFINER` and `SET search_path = ''`;
2. schema-qualifies every non-catalog relation and the ltree equality/containment operators;
3. preserves the four-key JSON response, limit fallback/clamp, and subtree filtering;
4. enumerates all same-name overloads and revokes PUBLIC/anon/authenticated/service_role EXECUTE;
5. explicitly re-revokes the canonical untrusted roles;
6. grants only the canonical signature to `service_role`.

Historical migrations were not modified, deleted, or rewritten.

## Final-catalog test design

The PostgreSQL SQL test first inspects the untouched final catalog produced by complete migration replay, before any remediation reapplication. It asserts canonical existence/signature/result/owner/security/search-path, all-overload ACLs, service-only canonical execution, and unchanged underlying privilege bounds.

It then proves anon denial, authenticated-own denial, authenticated-other denial, service-role success, field-by-field user A/B isolation, exact response keys, null/zero limit fallback, 50 clamp, and topic subtree filtering.

## Overload behavior test design

A separate transaction creates a synthetic `(text,ltree,integer)` overload and proves it initially has default PUBLIC EXECUTE inherited by anon/authenticated. It then reapplies only the remediation migration, proves untrusted EXECUTE is removed and service_role is not granted the noncanonical overload, and rolls back.

The migration-order Jest contract detects later same-name definitions across languages, return types, and signatures; direct or blanket FUNCTION/ROUTINE grants; mutable `ALTER FUNCTION/ROUTINE` search paths; missing true all-overload iteration/dynamic revoke; service-role ACL drift; unqualified live relations/helpers/operators; and underlying-table grant expansion.

An additional broad workspace batch exposed one pre-existing inline snapshot mismatch in `api/learning/__tests__/workspace-read-service.test.js` (`artifact_inbox_item` now includes `user_id`). This PR has no diff in that module or snapshot; the owner-bound workspace suites above pass. The unrelated snapshot was not rewritten.

items.title: security: enforce auth and rate limits on direct RAG routes
items.body:
## Root cause

`api/rag/ask.js` and `api/rag/search.js` were callable as file-based/serverless handlers without inheriting `api/index.js` gateway controls. They normalized input and called `executeAskAI` directly, so direct entrypoints bypassed JWT authentication and `rag_ai_default_v1` rate limiting.

## Direct exposure analysis

- `api/rag/ask.js`: direct handler had method validation, normalization, `executeAskAI`, and RAG telemetry only; no auth or rate-limit guard.
- `api/rag/search.js`: same direct-entry exposure and the same `executeAskAI` pipeline.
- Repository callers found: the central gateway loads both handlers through `api/_runtime/handler-loader.js`; focused handler tests import them directly. No `api/rag/chat.js` was changed or added.

## Deployment topology analysis

The repository has a central Node gateway (`api/index.js`) plus file-based `api/**` handlers. The registry maps `/api/rag/ask` and `/api/rag/search` to the two direct files. No deployment manifest in the repository was changed; direct handler exposure is therefore treated as a possible file-based/serverless deployment surface and is now fail-closed at the handler boundary.

## Affected handlers and gateway contract

Affected handlers are `/api/rag/ask` (`rag-ask`) and `/api/rag/search` (`rag-search`). Both canonical registry entries specify `jwt_required`, `authMode: authenticated`, and `rateLimitPolicyId: rag_ai_default_v1`. The effective policy is 10 authenticated-user requests/minute and 5 IP requests/minute, with a 60-second window and matching burst limits.

Before this change, the gateway order was method check → auth → rate limit → handler, while direct calls performed only method check. The gateway now and direct handlers now use one shared enforcement path in that same auth-before-rate-limit order.

## Shared guard and double-enforcement prevention

`api/lib/security/route-security-guard.js` is the single enforcement path. It calls the existing `requireAuth`, `applyRateLimitGuard`, canonical security failure helpers, degraded-rate-limit logging, and the existing 429 envelope with `Retry-After`. Direct handlers resolve their own route object from the route registry; they do not copy limits or policy objects. Missing, malformed, or mismatched direct route security contracts fail closed.

The guard stores auth and rate-limit promises in module-private request-object `WeakMap` state keyed by the canonical route object. Therefore gateway → handler invocation, repeated guard calls, and concurrent reuse of the same request do not repeat downstream auth lookup or consume a rate-limit token twice. No request header, query, body, cookie, or external marker is trusted as a completion signal.

## Auth and rate-limit behavior before/after

- Missing, malformed, invalid, expired, or configuration-failed auth now returns the canonical 401/500 security envelope before `executeAskAI`; auth rejection does not consume rate limit or record RAG model telemetry.
- Auth success sets and preserves `req.auth_context`, `req.auth_user_id`, and `req.auth_user`; client-provided `user_id` values do not override verified identity.
- Allowed authenticated calls preserve existing input normalization, response shapes, RAG pipeline behavior, and telemetry behavior.
- Denied calls return 429 with `Retry-After >= 1`, do not call `executeAskAI`, and do not record model-call telemetry.
- Degraded-but-allowed rate limiting retains existing logging/degrade semantics.

## Tests and results

Passed locally with mocked provider/retrieval boundaries and no remote Supabase:

- Direct route security: 16 tests.
- Shared route-security guard: 7 tests.
- Registry policy matrix, collision, and auth-context tests: included in a 45-test focused security/telemetry/auth run; all passed.
- Gateway security baseline/depth, shared rate limit, and API route integration: 22 tests; all passed.
- RAG ask/search characterization: 56 tests; all passed.
- Telemetry/auth middleware tests: 9 tests; all passed.
- ESLint on all changed JavaScript: passed.
- Workflow YAML parse: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `npm run workflow:codex-preflight -- --json`: passed with the expected dirty-worktree warning before commit; final clean-state preflight is included in handoff.

The first sandbox attempt at listener-based tests failed with `listen EPERM`; the same tests were rerun in the approved controlled environment and passed. No real embedding, retrieval, LLM, or provider call was made.

## GitHub Actions checks

Changed paths are under `api/**`, which already triggers API Route Integration Gate, Security Depth Gate, Security Baseline Gate, Shared Rate Limit Gate, and the repository-wide Lint Gate. No workflow path-filter change was necessary. CI remains GitHub-hosted and does not use repository secrets or self-hosted execution for this change.

## Review thread status

New PR; no review threads yet.

## Remaining limitations

This change hardens the repository's direct handler trust boundary. Deployment-specific routing outside this repository is not modified or independently verified. The change intentionally does not address the separately excluded RLS, privilege-escalation, cross-user view, recommendation, or RAG-log findings, and does not change retrieval, embedding, provider, prompt, ranking, response contracts, schema, or product behavior.

No remote Supabase was connected to or modified.

items.title: security: harden rubric extraction relations with RLS
items.body:
## Root cause

`supabase/migrations/20260214120000_b1_rubric_extraction.sql` created three sensitive tables and one publishing view in Supabase's exposed `public` schema without enabling or forcing RLS, without object-specific revokes, and without a security-invoker view option.

The later migration `20260219100000_fix_authenticated_grants_and_force_rls.sql` first revoked legacy blanket grants, then executed `GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO authenticated`. Because the B1 relations already existed, the effective final catalog restored direct authenticated SELECT on all three tables and the owner-executed view. The tables had no policies, so the grant exposed all rows rather than enforcing a row boundary.

## Relation inventory

| Relation | Type | Owner before | Sensitive contents |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `public.vlm_ms_jobs` | table | `postgres` | storage keys, extraction/provider versions, locks, failures, mutable queue status |
| `public.vlm_ms_runs` | table | `postgres` | run configuration, counts, failure summaries, operational audit state |
| `public.rubric_points` | table | `postgres` | authoritative rubric content/status, dependencies, raw model JSON, hashes and provider metadata |
| `public.rubric_points_ready_v1` | view | `postgres` | 21-column online-marking publishing contract for ready rows |

Historical definitions and later ALTERs were audited in migration order. The only later table changes are the duplicated Phase 2 additions of `is_cao`, `symbolic_rule`, and `accuracy_policy` to `rubric_points`. There was no later RLS, ACL, policy, owner, or view-security hardening before this change.

## Effective ACL and RLS before and after

### Before

| Relation | RLS | FORCE | PUBLIC | anon | authenticated | service_role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vlm_ms_jobs` | off | off | none | none | SELECT | none |
| `vlm_ms_runs` | off | off | none | none | SELECT | none |
| `rubric_points` | off | off | none | none | SELECT | none |
| `rubric_points_ready_v1` | n/a | n/a | none | none | SELECT | none |

All four relations had no column ACL. The three tables had no RLS policies. There were no checked-in default privileges. Earlier legacy migrations contained four blanket authenticated table grants; the later 20260219 migration removed their writes but deliberately restored blanket SELECT, which produced the effective exposure above.

### After

| Relation | RLS | FORCE | PUBLIC | anon | authenticated | service_role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vlm_ms_jobs` | on | on | none | none | none | none |
| `vlm_ms_runs` | on | on | none | none | none | none |
| `rubric_points` | on | on | none | none | none | SELECT |
| `rubric_points_ready_v1` | security invoker | n/a | none | none | none | SELECT |

The migration revokes all table privileges and every current column privilege from PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, and service_role before explicitly restoring only the two resolver reads. It creates no policy and grants no trusted write through the Data API.

## View security model before and after

Before, `rubric_points_ready_v1` was a normal owner-executed view with no reloptions. Authenticated callers had direct SELECT and could execute using the owner security context.

After, the same relation has `security_invoker=true`. The relation name, 21 column names/order, `concat_ws(':', extractor_version, provider, model, prompt_version)` source-version expression, and `status = 'ready'` filter are unchanged. The view does not expose `raw_json`, `response_sha256`, or `parse_flags`. PUBLIC, anon, and authenticated have no view SELECT; service_role has SELECT and must also use its explicit base-table SELECT.

## Caller inventory and database identities

- `api/marking/lib/rubric-resolver-v1.js`
  - reads latest version metadata from `rubric_points`;
  - reads publishable points from `rubric_points_ready_v1`;
  - receives the server-only service-role client from `evaluate-v1`.
- `api/marking/evaluate-v1.js` and the ledger/marking call chain use `getServiceClient()`; PG compatibility mode substitutes the direct `DATABASE_URL` PostgreSQL client.
- `scripts/ms/ms_batch_process.py` uses a psycopg2 pool created from `DATABASE_URL` / `SUPABASE_DB_URL`; it claims and updates jobs and creates/updates runs.
- `scripts/ms/ms_persist.py` uses that same direct pool; it upserts rubric points and updates job status.
- `scripts/ms/seed_ms_jobs.py`, `seed_b1_gate_fixture.py`, dependency resolver, contract validator, QC sampler, B1 gate, Phase 1 seed/audit scripts, and rubric governance scripts use direct PostgreSQL URLs.
- Checked-in local/CI database URLs use the `postgres` role. Clean catalog verification proves that role is the table owner, superuser, and `BYPASSRLS`; its direct worker/seed/governance behavior remains compatible with forced RLS.
- Resolver/evaluate tests use mocks. DB constraint/idempotency tests use direct PostgreSQL.
- No dedicated non-bypass worker role exists in migrations or checked-in configuration.
- No frontend/browser file references these four relations. Frontend Supabase boundary tests also prohibit direct Vite Supabase credentials.

## Why authenticated direct access is unnecessary

The browser does not query these relations. Online marking resolves rubrics server-side with the trusted service-role client, and extraction/governance paths use direct PostgreSQL connections. A view name containing “ready” or “publishing” is therefore not evidence of a browser/public contract. Keeping the relations service-only preserves every proven caller without exposing raw rubric or operational state.

## Migration strategy

Added the forward-only migration:

`supabase/migrations/20260712070730_harden_rubric_extraction_relations_rls.sql`

It:

1. enables and forces RLS on all three tables;
2. revokes all table privileges from PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, and service_role;
3. dynamically removes current column ACLs for the four protected relations;
4. sets `security_invoker=true` on the existing view without recreating it;
5. revokes all view privileges from the same roles;
6. grants only `rubric_points SELECT` and ready-view `SELECT` to service_role.

The historical B1 migration was not modified, deleted, or rewritten. No `USING (true)` or `WITH CHECK (true)` policy was added.

## Service-role least privilege

The service-role client needs table-level SELECT on `rubric_points` for version selection and SELECT on `rubric_points_ready_v1` for ready points. It receives no job/run privilege and no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, REFERENCES, or TRIGGER privilege. Extraction writes were not moved to service_role because the caller audit found no such path.

## Direct worker compatibility

The proven direct PostgreSQL identity is `postgres`. PostgreSQL superusers and roles with `BYPASSRLS` bypass RLS even when FORCE is enabled. The role test performs real job insert/claim update, run insert/update, and rubric persistence as `postgres`, then verifies the persisted state inside a transaction. If a future deployment introduces a non-bypass dedicated worker role, it will need a separately reviewed narrow trusted-role design; this PR does not invent one or compensate with authenticated access.

## Final-catalog and role test design

`tests/evidence-ledger/rubric-extraction-rls-security.sql` runs immediately after complete migration replay and before any remediation reapplication. It asserts:

- canonical object types, owners, RLS/FORCE flags, ACLs, column ACLs, and absence of policies;
- exact service-role privileges and absence of extra privileges;
- explicit `security_invoker=true`, exact 21-column view contract, ready-only filter, and sensitive-column exclusions;
- anon and authenticated SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE denial on all tables and ready-view denial;
- a temporary anon view grant still cannot bypass base-table privileges, proving invoker behavior;
- service-role base version selection and ready-view reads succeed while draft/needs-review rows remain hidden;
- service_role cannot update rubric data or inspect jobs/runs;
- direct `postgres` worker operations still work;
- every fixture and temporary grant rolls back.

A remediation re-run was tested later in a cloned independent database, never before the untouched final-catalog assertion.

## Migration-order regression design

`tests/evidence-ledger/rubric-extraction-rls-security-contract.test.js` reads every migration in filename order. It validates final effective actions and fails on later:

- RLS disable or NO FORCE;
- untrusted exact, blanket, or column grants;
- default-PUBLIC or explicitly untrusted permissive policies;
- service-role privilege drift;
- same-name table replacement without ENABLE plus FORCE;
- view replacement without security invoker;
- view column-order/contract changes;
- raw JSON/hash/parse flag exposure;
- removal of the ready-only filter;
- explicit security-invoker disable/reset.

Mutation cases prove those detectors reject representative future regressions rather than only grepping the remediation file.

## Exact local tests and results

- Fresh `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` clean replay:
  - 93 migrations applied;
  - only `20260118090900_008_rag_log_retention.sql` skipped because the image lacks `pg_cron`, matching the existing CI rule;
  - final catalog/SET ROLE SQL: pass.
- Independent cloned-database remediation re-run plus full role SQL: pass.
- Migration-order contract: 1 suite, 16/16 tests passed.
- All marking + evidence-ledger + PG compat + Supabase audit-core JavaScript:
  - 29 suites passed;
  - 478 tests passed;
  - 0 snapshots.
- All `tests/test_ms_*.py` plus `tests/test_marking_evaluate_v1_integration.py`:
  - 326 tests passed.
- `scripts/phase2/check_db_contract.py`: pass.
- `scripts/phase2/run_migration_smoke.py`: pass.
- Supabase Security Advisors on the disposable final database: exit 0.
  - no `rls_disabled_in_public` for `vlm_ms_jobs`, `vlm_ms_runs`, or `rubric_points`;
  - no `security_definer_view` for `rubric_points_ready_v1`;
  - the three deny-by-default tables produce expected INFO-only `rls_enabled_no_policy` entries.
- Supabase CLI `db lint`: attempted, but the pgvector image could not enable `pgsql_check`; this PR does not claim db lint passed.

## GitHub Actions status

Final status for head `b8547537ab63d07ae5070a95180d278367356e4c`: 10 jobs passed and 1 event-gated job was skipped; no job failed or remained pending. Passed jobs: `Rubric Extraction RLS Security Contract`, `DB Contract + Migration Smoke`, `Mark Decision RPC Security Contract`, `Evidence Context RPC Security Contract`, `Backend/platform ESLint`, `ESLint`, `Boundary Contract`, `Boundary DB Guardrail`, `S1 Contract Gate`, and `PR Workflow Trust Boundary`. `Trusted Repository Workflow Trust Boundary` was skipped by its expected pull-request event condition. items.title: security: make user profile roles server-controlled
items.body:
## Findings

This single narrow PR fixes the two Codex Security findings that share the same database trust-boundary root cause:

1. `New role column enables self-service admin escalation`
2. `User-controlled profile role enables privilege escalation`

It does not address recommendation RLS, cross-user security/study views, RAG log RLS, or other Supabase advisor findings.

Base SHA: `fc49e7a3e517926ac1094562b8759388c1970da9` (`origin/main` after PRs #1531, #1532, #1533, and #1534 were merged).

## Root cause

`20260118091530_add_user_profiles_email.sql` added `public.user_profiles.role TEXT` without a default, NOT NULL, allowed-value check, column ACL hardening, or an immutable-role boundary. The original policies allowed users to insert and update their own profile. `20260219100000_fix_authenticated_grants_and_force_rls.sql` later derived authenticated writes from those PUBLIC policies, leaving the final replayed ACL as `authenticated=SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE` on every profile column.

The row predicate prevented cross-user writes but did not constrain columns. A real pre-fix `SET ROLE authenticated` transaction proved user A could update its own `role` to `admin`, change `status/password_hash`, and insert a new profile with `role=admin`. The existing role-history trigger then recorded the attacker as `changed_by`, turning the escalation itself into apparently valid audit history.

## Historical and effective schema audit

Historical `user_profiles` definitions and ALTERs:

- `20260118090000_001_initial_schema.sql`: `id`, `name`, `avatar_url`, `school`, `grade_level`, `subjects`, `preferences`, `created_at`, `updated_at`; RLS plus own SELECT/UPDATE/INSERT policies; updated-at trigger; `auth.users` profile trigger.
- `20260118091100_010_study_hub_extension.sql`: `learning_preferences`, `learning_goals`, `study_schedule`, `performance_metrics`.
- `20260118091530_add_user_profiles_email.sql`: `email`, `role`.
- `20260118091600_014_auth_system.sql`: reset/verification/password/last-login/status fields, indexes, role-history trigger, and legacy blanket authenticated grants.
- `20260219100000_fix_authenticated_grants_and_force_rls.sql`: revoke blanket ACLs, restore blanket SELECT, derive authenticated writes from PUBLIC/authenticated policies, and FORCE RLS on policy-bearing tables.

Final pre-fix catalog had 23 columns. `role` was nullable `text`, had no default, and had no CHECK. No column had an `attacl`. `user_profiles` owner was `postgres`; RLS and FORCE RLS were both on because of the later blanket hardening migration.

## Effective role schema before / after

| Contract | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Type | `text` | `text` |
| Default | none | `'student'::text` |
| Nullable | yes | no |
| Allowed values | unconstrained | validated `student`, `teacher`, `moderator`, `admin` CHECK |
| Existing NULL/blank | left unchanged | normalized to `student` |
| Existing allowed case/whitespace variants | left unchanged | trimmed and lower-cased |
| Existing unknown role | accepted | migration fails closed and prints the distinct unknown values |
| Insert/update guard | none | fixed-search-path SECURITY INVOKER trigger; only `postgres`/`service_role` can set privileged roles |

The migration takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock before normalization and contract changes. It never maps an unknown value to a privileged role.

## Final ACL / RLS before / after

### Before

- owner: `postgres`
- RLS: enabled and forced
- table ACL: `authenticated=SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE`; `anon=none`; clean replay had no explicit `service_role` grant
- column ACL: none, so authenticated table UPDATE covered all 23 columns
- policies (all historical policies targeted `{public}`): own SELECT, own UPDATE, own INSERT
- role history: authenticated SELECT only at table ACL, but a PUBLIC admin/moderator `FOR ALL` policy remained and could become writable after a future grant

### After

- owner remains `postgres`; RLS and FORCE RLS are explicitly reasserted
- authenticated has only table-level SELECT plus an owner-scoped `TO authenticated` SELECT policy
- authenticated and anon have no table- or column-level INSERT/UPDATE privilege; there is no self-insert or self-update policy
- service_role has exactly SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE on `user_profiles`; no DELETE/TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER
- all surviving column ACLs for PUBLIC/anon/authenticated/service_role are swept before the explicit table grants
- `user_role_history` is trigger-only for writes: non-owner table and column writes are revoked; authenticated keeps owner-scoped SELECT only; the legacy admin/moderator manage policy is removed
- trigger-only functions have EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, and service_role

## Why profile writes are service-only

The caller audit found no supported browser-side Supabase write to `user_profiles`. `src/services/userProfileService.js` sends authenticated requests to `/api/user-profile`; it does not import or call a frontend Supabase client. Therefore this PR removes authenticated INSERT/UPDATE entirely instead of preserving an unused direct-write surface.

The server profile route already binds `id` to verified auth context and uses an explicit allowlist: `name`, `avatar_url`, `school`, `grade_level`, `subjects`, and `learningPreferences -> preferences`. New tests prove `body.user_id`, `id`, `role`, `status`, password/verification fields, and `reputation` cannot pass through PUT or POST profile writes.

## Role consumer inventory

Database consumers of `user_profiles.role`:

- admin access to all login attempts
- admin access to all sessions
- admin management of user permissions
- historical admin/moderator role-history management policy (removed here)
- admin access to all devices
- admin access to all security events

Application consumers:

- `api/middleware/auth.js`: database profile role -> roleLevel, permission set, admin checks, and moderator ownership bypass
- `api/lib/security/auth-context.js`: gateway role context
- `api/learning/ms-source-reveal/assets.js`: teacher/admin preview role
- frontend auth normalization/display: UI state only; not an authorization boundary

No checked-in role-management route, public SECURITY DEFINER role RPC, or product role-change endpoint exists.

## Writer / caller inventory

| Caller | Effective caller | Writes | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| public registration in `api/auth/index.js` | service_role backend | profile insert fixed to `student` | preserved |
| login / verification / reset / password change | service_role backend | last_login, status, password and verification/reset fields | preserved by exact service SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE grant |
| `/api/user-profile` PUT/POST | service_role backend after verified JWT | explicit non-sensitive profile allowlist; verified subject id | preserved and regression-tested |
| `auth.users` trigger | postgres SECURITY DEFINER | `id`, metadata `name`, literal `student` role | hardened with fixed search_path and schema qualification |
| Phase 1 fixture seed | direct postgres fixture | literal `student` | compatible |
| anon/authenticated Data API | untrusted PostgREST roles | historical direct INSERT/UPDATE | removed |
| trusted role mutation | service_role or direct postgres operator SQL | role only under CHECK/guard | allowed and audited |

No service-role route accepts `body.role`; no generic `update(req.body)` or profile object spread was found. No caller maps client-supplied metadata into database role.

## Registration analysis

PR #1475 behavior remains intact: admin, moderator, teacher, and missing-role registration inputs all create and return `student`. The `auth.users` trigger now also writes literal `student`; it reads only the display name from `raw_user_meta_data` and never reads metadata role.

## Profile confused-deputy analysis

`/api/user-profile` uses the service client, so its verified identity and field allowlist are the real application boundary. The route ignores caller-selected ids and all authorization, credential, verification, status, login, and reputation fields. Static and runtime tests cover both PUT and POST. No public admin role-change endpoint was added.

## Token and session trust analysis

Custom access and refresh JWTs currently contain a role field for compatibility, but production authorization does not trust it:

- `authenticateRequest()` verifies the token subject, reloads the active database profile on every request, and derives permissions from the database role.
- refresh verifies the tracked refresh session, reloads the database profile, and signs new tokens from the current database role.
- tests prove a forged admin access claim remains student, a forged admin refresh claim produces a student access token, and the same access token immediately gains/loses permissions after a trusted database promotion/demotion.

The optional Supabase Auth fallback previously trusted `user_metadata.role` before `app_metadata.role`. It now requires an active protected database profile and uses only that profile role. MS source reveal no longer falls back to either metadata role. `AUTH_LOCAL_TEST_MODE=true` now fails closed when `NODE_ENV=production`.

Because every production role authorization path is database-authoritative, role downgrade is immediate and does not depend on access-token expiry or refresh-session revocation. This PR does not add a product role-change endpoint or a new session-revocation workflow.

## Role history design

`public.trigger_user_role_history()` remains SECURITY DEFINER so the append-only trigger can write while direct history writes stay revoked. It now has `SET search_path = ''`, schema-qualified relations, and writes only when `OLD.role IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.role`. The trigger is narrowed to `AFTER UPDATE OF role`.

`changed_by` is `auth.uid()` when a trusted service establishes request identity; it is NULL for service-key or direct operator SQL. Tests prove one successful trusted change produces one accurate old/new history row, an unchanged role writes nothing, failed untrusted changes write nothing, and direct history forgery is denied.

The role guard is separately SECURITY INVOKER, so its `current_user` check observes real `SET ROLE authenticated`/`service_role` semantics rather than a definer identity.

## Forward-only migration strategy

- new migration: `20260712085844_make_user_profile_roles_server_controlled.sql`
- generated with `supabase migration new`
- no historical migration changed
- normalization and unknown-role preflight run under an exclusive table lock
- explicit table and column ACL cleanup precedes exact re-grants
- owner-scoped SELECT policy is recreated with `TO authenticated`
- role guard, auth-user trigger, history relation, history function, and triggers are hardened in one transaction

## Exact local tests and results

- complete clean `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` replay: 95 migration files discovered; 94 applied in order; only `20260118090900_008_rag_log_retention.sql` skipped because pg_cron is unavailable, matching existing CI policy; exit 0
- final catalog plus real SET ROLE SQL: pass; all fixtures ran inside a transaction and rolled back
- legacy-data probes: NULL/blank -> student, ` ADMIN ` -> admin; unknown `owner` aborted with the expected fail-closed exception
- user-profile role migration-order/application static contract: 25/25 passed
- auth productionization: 24/24 passed
- focused auth-context/profile/MS reveal/middleware suites: 49/49 passed
- API Route Integration + Security Depth/Baseline + security middleware: 102/102 passed
- existing mark-decision/evidence-context/rubric/user-profile static contracts plus Supabase audit-core: 89/89 passed
- existing mark-decision RPC, evidence-context RPC, and rubric extraction SQL contracts: all exit 0
- DB Contract: pass, 6 checks
- Migration Smoke: pass, 3 checks (raw replay database was given the equivalent local `supabase_migrations` tracking row)
- deterministic Security Baseline gate: pass
- deterministic Security Depth gate: pass, 85 checks, 0 failures
- deterministic API Route Integration summary: pass
- workflow trust tests: 10/10 passed
- review follow-up (`auth-context`, auth productionization, and role migration-order contract): 3/3 suites, 58/58 tests passed; `PGRST116` remains the missing-profile 401 path and unexpected database errors now produce a structured 500
- official local Supabase Security Advisors: exit 0; 48 unrelated legacy warnings, 0 target findings for `user_profiles`, `user_role_history`, or the three hardened trigger functions
- Supabase CLI db lint: attempted but not passed; the pgvector image cannot enable `pgsql_check` (`LegacyDbLintEnableCheckError`), and the extension is not available in the image
- ESLint on every changed JavaScript file: pass
- workflow YAML parse: pass
- `git diff --check`: pass
- preflight: branch/sync/workflow checks healthy; sparse checkout reports the three pre-existing `origin/main` report-index files as missing and therefore keeps the report-artifact guard in warning mode

## GitHub Actions status

Final head `a26c8e86898391a2504f15f1bef06663cc9018c9`: 16 checks passed and 1 check was skipped by design.

- passed: API Route Integration; Backend Consistency; Backend/platform ESLint; Boundary Contract; Boundary DB Guardrail; DB Contract + Migration Smoke; ESLint; Evidence Context RPC Security Contract; Mark Decision RPC Security Contract; PR Workflow Trust Boundary; Rubric Extraction RLS Security Contract; S1 Contract Gate; Security Baseline; Security Depth Gate; Shared Rate Limit Gate; User Profile Role Security Contract
- skipped: Trusted Repository Workflow Trust Boundary (the PR-specific trust-boundary job passed; the trusted-repository variant does not run for this draft PR event)
- failed/cancelled/pending: none

## Review thread status

One high-priority inline thread was opened on `api/lib/security/auth-context.js`: unexpected database profile errors were being masked as 401 authentication failures. Commit `a26c8e86898391a2504f15f1bef06663cc9018c9` distinguishes the expected `PGRST116` missing-row case from system/database failures and adds both regression branches. The original thread was replied to and resolved.

- total inline review threads: 1
- resolved: 1
- unresolved: 0
- outdated: 0
- top-level conversation comments: 0
- reviews: 1 external `COMMENTED` review plus the thread-resolution reply; no `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review

## Remaining limitations

- This PR intentionally does not redesign the auth system, split credential columns into a new relation, add product RBAC, add a role-management API, or change frontend UI.
- Existing owner-scoped profile SELECT semantics are unchanged; this finding is closed by removing untrusted writes and making authorization state server-controlled.
- Official local advisors still report 48 unrelated legacy function/extension/permissive-policy warnings; they are outside the named findings.
- The disposable image lacks pg_cron and pgsql_check.
- No remote catalog drift was inspected because this task prohibits connecting to remote Supabase.

## Remote and deployment statement

No production, staging, linked, or other remote Supabase environment was connected to or modified. No `supabase db push` was run. No real user, admin, profile, session, or role data was created or changed. The new migration has not been applied to any remote environment and is not deployed.

This PR must not be merged by the worker.

items.title: security: harden recommendation RLS and analytics access
items.body:
## Finding

Fixes exactly one Codex Security finding: **Migration unblocks unsafe recommendation RLS grants**.

This PR does not address the cross-user security/study view finding, RAG-log RLS, user_profiles disclosure, or other legacy Supabase advisor findings. It does not change the recommendation algorithm, public response contracts, frontend UI, or recommendation product logic.

## Base

- Actual PR base branch: `main`
- Actual base SHA: `d76a5812b760d6fefba83a807a553ae8f9f0162c`
- Verified base commit: `security: make user profile roles server-controlled (#1535)`
- Head: `93bddf08b1dd29e17f42b075239e72d2de7fba36`

## Root cause chain

The effective vulnerability is the ordered chain:

1. `20260118091200_011_recommendation_system.sql` created the old `recommendation_analytics` view with a `user_id` column and also introduced blanket authenticated grants.
2. `20260118091250_012_unblock_recommendation_analytics_view.sql` dropped that view when the old contract was detected.
3. The unblock allowed `20260118091500_013_recommendation_system_enhanced.sql` to finish, creating the enhanced recommendation relations, PUBLIC-applicable `"System can ..."` policies, unrestricted predicates, five exposed functions, a new global aggregate view, and additional blanket grants.
4. `20260219100000_fix_authenticated_grants_and_force_rls.sql` revoked old blanket grants but re-granted SELECT on all public tables and re-derived authenticated writes from PUBLIC/authenticated policies, preserving the dangerous effective catalog.

The unblock migration is not independently unsafe SQL; it enabled the later unsafe catalog state to become effective.

## Effective relation inventory

Full migration replay before remediation produced postgres-owned relations:

| Relation | Effective pre-fix state | Post-fix state |
|---|---|---|
| `user_learning_data` | FORCE RLS; authenticated SELECT/INSERT; PUBLIC owner + unrestricted system INSERT policies | service-only; service_role SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE |
| `recommendations` | FORCE RLS; authenticated SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; PUBLIC system ALL policy | service-only; service_role SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE |
| `user_learning_profiles` | FORCE RLS; authenticated SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; PUBLIC owner policy plus later authenticated/service policies | service-only; service_role SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE |
| `recommendation_feedback` | FORCE RLS; authenticated SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; multiple PUBLIC owner policies | service-only; service_role SELECT/INSERT |
| `content_similarity` | FORCE RLS; authenticated SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; PUBLIC read and system ALL policies | deny-by-default; no Data API role ACL |
| `learning_objectives` | FORCE RLS; authenticated SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; PUBLIC owner ALL policy | deny-by-default; no Data API role ACL |
| `recommendation_cache` | FORCE RLS; authenticated SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; PUBLIC system ALL plus `user_id IS NULL` read | service-only; service_role SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE |
| `algorithm_performance` | FORCE RLS; authenticated SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; PUBLIC system ALL policy | deny-by-default; no Data API role ACL |
| `recommendation_analytics` | owner-security view; authenticated SELECT; global cross-user aggregate | same 11-column aggregate contract; `security_invoker=true`; no Data API ACL |

Before remediation there were 19 effective policies on the eight target tables. After remediation there are zero policies: these are service-only tables and service_role uses BYPASSRLS plus explicit table ACL.

All table and column ACLs are reset for PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, and service_role before the exact service_role matrix is re-granted. service_role receives no TRUNCATE, REFERENCES, or TRIGGER privilege.

## recommendation_feedback effective schema

Complete replay confirms that the effective schema is the 011 definition because both 011 and 013 use `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`:

1. `id uuid`
2. `user_id uuid`
3. `recommendation_id uuid`
4. `feedback_type text`
5. `rating integer`
6. `comment text`
7. `created_at timestamptz`

The effective FK is `recommendation_id -> recommendation_history(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, not the 013 FK to `recommendations(id)`; `implicit_feedback` is absent. This PR deliberately does not rewrite that compatibility contract. The SQL fixture mirrors recommendation IDs into `recommendation_history` so service-role feedback ACL behavior is tested against the real schema.

## Caller inventory and database identities

| Caller | Identity | Required target access |
|---|---|---|
| `api/recommendations/index.js` | authenticated HTTP request; DB service_role | recommendations CRUD, cache CRUD, feedback INSERT |
| `api/recommendations/algorithm-engine.js` and orchestrator | server service_role | profiles SELECT, learning data SELECT, feedback SELECT |
| `api/recommendations/learning-data.js` | authenticated HTTP request; DB service_role | learning data CRUD |
| `api/recommendations/preferences.js` | authenticated HTTP request; DB service_role | profiles SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE |
| `api/auth/index.js` registration path | server service_role | profiles INSERT |
| `api/evidence/context.js` fallback | authenticated backend; DB service_role | profiles SELECT |
| `scripts/aggregation/aggregate-learner-profiles.js` | service-role batch job | profiles SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE |
| migrations / SQL verification | postgres trusted operator | owner/maintenance operations |
| tests | mock client or disposable postgres roles | contract verification only |

No checked-in runtime caller uses content_similarity, learning_objectives, algorithm_performance, recommendation_analytics, or any of the five target functions as direct RPC.

## Browser direct-access audit

Repo-wide searches found no frontend `supabase.from(...)` or RPC caller for these target objects. The current UI calls authenticated HTTP endpoints such as `/api/recommendations` and `/api/recommendations/preferences`. Therefore no authenticated browser relation privilege is retained.

## Service-role least-privilege matrix

| Relation | SELECT | INSERT | UPDATE | DELETE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| recommendations | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| recommendation_cache | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| user_learning_data | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| user_learning_profiles | yes | yes | yes | no |
| recommendation_feedback | yes | yes | no | no |
| content_similarity | no | no | no | no |
| learning_objectives | no | no | no | no |
| algorithm_performance | no | no | no | no |
| recommendation_analytics | no | n/a | n/a | n/a |

## Analytics view security model

The current global aggregate name and exact 11-column contract are preserved. It remains a cross-user behavioral aggregate and is not represented as user-scoped.

The migration sets `security_invoker=true`, revokes all privileges from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated/service_role, and grants no SELECT because no trusted caller exists. Tests also temporarily mis-grant view SELECT to authenticated and prove base-table ACL/RLS still blocks the aggregate.

The contract excludes `user_id`, feedback comments/implicit feedback, cache payload/metadata, and recommendation metadata.

## Function and overload audit

Effective pre-fix catalog:

- `update_cache_hit_count()`
- `cleanup_expired_recommendations()`
- `cleanup_expired_cache()`
- `update_learning_profile_from_activity()`
- `calculate_user_engagement_score(uuid,text)`

All five were postgres-owned SECURITY INVOKER functions with mutable search_path and default PUBLIC EXECUTE, making anon/authenticated/service_role effective executors. No real direct RPC caller was found.

The remediation preserves INVOKER semantics, fixes `search_path = ''`, schema-qualifies target relations and relevant built-ins, and revokes EXECUTE from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated/service_role across every same-name overload. Trigger functions receive no direct service_role EXECUTE. Postgres retains owner maintenance ability. Transactional tests prove both trigger paths still execute through legitimate service-role table operations.

## API confused-deputy analysis

- All three direct handlers call the shared trusted-auth resolver; gateway registry contracts remain `jwt_required`.
- Verified identity is sourced from `req.auth_user_id` / trusted auth context; body/query `user_id` is ignored.
- Cache keys include verified user ID.
- Recommendation owner lookup and update/delete mutations filter both recommendation ID and verified user ID.
- Feedback submission first resolves an owned recommendation, and inserted feedback `user_id` is the verified user.
- Learning-data POST forces `user_id`; PUT/DELETE perform owner lookup and repeat owner filters; update spread is whitelist-derived.
- Preference and learning-profile writes use verified user ID and composite `user_id,subject_code` conflict identity.
- Permission-denied cache reads/writes/clears now rethrow and fail closed; ordinary cache-miss/degradation behavior and response contracts are unchanged.

## Migration strategy

A single forward-only migration, `20260712195154_harden_recommendation_rls_and_analytics_access.sql`, applies after all existing migrations. Historical migrations 011/012/013 are unchanged. It:

- enables and forces RLS on all eight base tables;
- resets table and column ACLs;
- drops all policies from the service-only target tables;
- restores only the proven service_role table matrix;
- makes the existing analytics view security-invoker and private;
- hardens all five functions and sweeps same-name overload ACLs.

## Final-catalog and role-test design

The SQL test runs after complete migration replay and, before any remediation reapplication, asserts owners, relation kinds, ENABLE/FORCE RLS, table ACL, column ACL, zero policies, exact service privileges, view definition/columns/options, feedback schema/FK, function owner/security/search_path/ACL, and trigger wiring.

Transactional role fixtures prove anon/authenticated denials, security-invoker behavior under a temporary bad view grant, legitimate service-role CRUD, verified-user query filtering, cache/profile trigger behavior, and denial of unused service privileges/functions. A synthetic same-name overload is created, the exact migration body is reapplied inside the transaction, the ACL sweep is verified, and the transaction is rolled back.

## Migration-order regression design

The static contract reads every ordered migration and includes mutation cases for:

- RLS DISABLE / NO FORCE;
- target or blanket untrusted table grants;
- blanket function grants;
- column ACL restoration;
- any policy on service-only target tables, including missing-TO and true predicates;
- service_role privilege drift;
- analytics invoker loss, untrusted grants, contract expansion, or sensitive columns;
- protected-function redefinition/search_path/EXECUTE drift;
- body/query user ID acceptance, owner-filter removal, cache-key user removal, feedback owner-check removal, and learning-data owner-check removal.

## Exact local tests and results

- Recommendation static migration/application contract: **1 suite, 30 tests passed**.
- Cross-security migration detector coexistence after CI feedback: **3 suites, 90 tests passed** (Recommendation RLS, Evidence Context RPC, User Profile Role).
- Recommendation productionization + trusted-deputy + orchestrator: **3 suites, 23 tests passed**.
- Route registry policy/collision + auth-context + route-security guard: **4 suites, 93 tests passed**.

The retained contracts expose only their historical summary columns. Full replay before remediation: all three were `relkind='v'`, owner `postgres`, empty reloptions, authenticated effective SELECT, no PUBLIC/anon/service_role privilege, and no column ACL.

Full replay after remediation: all three remain `relkind='v'`, owner `postgres`, preserve exact column order, have `{security_invoker=true}`, and their relation ACL contains only the owner. ## Underlying RLS / policy audit

Final replay confirmed all 10 dependencies are postgres-owned with ENABLE + FORCE RLS:

| Surface | Database identity | Target-view caller |
| --- | --- | --- |
| browser `src/**` Supabase `.from` / RPC / REST | anon or authenticated | none |
| API routes / server services | service_role after verified auth | none |
| scripts / dashboards / reporting | service_role or postgres/direct DB | none |
| migrations | postgres/direct DB | historical definitions/grants only |
| tests/mocks | mock/test | audit fixture reference only; no runtime query |

`/api/user-profile` calls `requireAuth`, derives the verified user ID, and filters direct base-table queries by it. - `ALTER VIEW ... SET (security_invoker=true)`;

- owner: `postgres`
- columns: `id, created_at, user_id, query_text, subject_code, paper_code, topic_id, mode, match_count, duration_ms, top_score, top_chunk_id, items, degraded, retries`

- FORCE RLS: enabled by the later repository-wide hardening migration

- columns/defaults/indexes are unchanged
- RLS and FORCE RLS are enabled
- every policy on `public.rag_search_logs` is removed
- PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, and service_role have no table privilege

There is no legitimate browser direct logging or log-reading requirement. Browser code calls authenticated server RAG routes only. The migration-order/runtime contract scans the entire browser source tree and rejects future references to the table or either function.

History contained:

Post-fix: the same 13-argument argument/return contract, SECURITY INVOKER, `search_path=''`, schema-qualified table, and no PUBLIC/anon/authenticated/service_role EXECUTE. A dynamic `pg_proc` sweep revokes all four principals from every same-name overload.

Historical `rag_search_logs_purge(integer DEFAULT 90)` was SECURITY DEFINER, had no fixed search_path or validation, and default-created PUBLIC EXECUTE. A pg_cron-enabled isolated Supabase Postgres replay confirmed the function was executable by PUBLIC/anon/authenticated/service_role.

- Direct ask/search routes require the #1533 JWT boundary before RAG or telemetry work.
- Verified identity is stored on `req.auth_user_id` / `req.auth_user`.
- Ask now explicitly strips both `body.user_id` and `body.userId`; search already builds a canonical allowlisted input object.
- Query-string user identity is ignored.
- There is no service-role legacy log RPC forwarding path, so callers cannot currently substitute `in_user_id`.
- Current telemetry does not persist raw query text or result items to this table; it hashes normalized queries.

| Capability | PUBLIC | anon | authenticated | service_role | postgres/owner |

| noncanonical logger overload EXECUTE | no | no | no | no | owner only |
| purge EXECUTE | no | no | no | no | yes |

- enables and forces RLS;
- drops all existing table policies;
- revokes table and column privileges from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated/service_role;

The SQL test proves:

- `purge(90)` deletes a 100-day row and preserves 2-day/12-hour rows.
- `purge(1)` deletes the 2-day row and preserves the 12-hour row.
- 0, negative, NULL, and 3651 are rejected with SQLSTATE 22023.
- canonical log fields/return behavior remain compatible for owner operations.

## Overload-sweep test
